newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S., China extend maritime accord.
newsitem.headline: U.S., China extend maritime accord.

text.p: China and the United States have extended for another year a maritime agreement governing treatment of each other's ships, the U.S. embassy said on Tuesday.

The agreement, which covers issues including reciprocal treatment for each other's ships and notification procedures for entering ports, will be extended until June 15, 1998. It was first signed in 1988 and had been extended previously.
The agreement underscores the strong commitment of both countries to strengthen and expand commercial cooperation in the maritime sector, the statement said.

U.S. and Chinese carriers have made substantial investments in each other's maritime sectors and provide a broad range of related services. The extension of the accord will promote the development of these commercial interests, the statement said.
